column1: # The only code path that can WRITE into 0xFF5C06-0xFF5C44:
#   The USB EP1 bulk-OUT byte-copy loop at 0x055684/0x055688:
#     055678  mov.w  @0xFFBA6C,r5        ; write index
#     05567e  add.l  #0xFF5806,er5       ; dst = 0xFF5806 + index   (register-indirect, NOT absolute)
#     055684  mov.b  @0xFFEE10,r4l       ; read EPDR1 (USB EP1 data)
#     055688  mov.b  r4l,@er5            ; <-- store; @er5 can land in 0xFF5C06-0xFF5C44 on overrun
#     05569e  cmp.w  #0x400,r5           ; wrap check AFTER the packet copy
#     0556a2  bcs    loc_556C0           ; index<0x400 -> re-arm; else wrap to 0
#   On a misaligned upload (short packet mid-stream) the index can reach up to 0x3FF, then a full 64-byte
#   packet copies to 0xFF5806+0x3FF .. +0x43E = up to 0xFF5C44 before the 0x400 wrap check fires.
#   This is the exact 63-byte overrun I12 doc-64 flagged. It is a bug consequence, not an owner.
